title: Marginal-Nonuniform Multiclass Learning
claim: Learnability notions form a nested hierarchy, with each broader learning rate characterized by a weaker combinatorial condition than the stricter one inside it.
layout: 1 panel, nested rounded rectangles, outside-in, characterizations beside each level label
description: A single Venn-style diagram of four nested rounded rectangles that stand for learnability regimes. The innermost red box reads 'DS(C) < ∞ ⟺ 1/n-uniform', the classical PAC case. A purple box around it reads 'countable union of DS classes ⟺', labeled 1/n-marginal-nonuniform. A pink box reads 'no strong uDSE seq. ⟺'. The outermost pale-blue box reads 'no infinite DSL tree ⟺', labeled 1/n-universal. A light-blue box labeled 1/n-concept-nonuniform overlaps the marginal-nonuniform region without being nested inside it. Small dots mark Propositions 10, 12 and 13, which are separation results. Colors shift from saturated red at the center to pale lavender outside, so the eye goes to the center first. Equivalence arrows and mathematical notation appear throughout.
caption: Simplified visualization of the learnability landscape in the considered learning setups.
abstract: We study the problem of multiclass classification within the framework of marginal-nonuniform learning, where the constants in the learning rate may depend on the unknown marginal distribution generating the unlabeled data, but not on the target concept. This notion naturally lies between classical PAC learning, where the constants are independent of both the marginal distribution and the target concept, and more recent universal learning, where the constants may depend on both. We give a complete characterization of the optimal marginal-nonuniform learning rates, establishing a fundamental trichotomy: exponential, linear, and arbitrarily slow rates. This characterization is witnessed by a new combinatorial dimension, termed the uncentered DS-eluder dimension. A key ingredient in the upper-bound proofs is a set of new distributional exhaustion lemmas that exploit the sequential nature of this dimension and may be of independent interest.
